properties.state: {"kind":"functional","lineage":"derived","name":"In a physical design, a proposed change to one part returns its redo list: every part, calculation, trade and drawing that depends on it, grouped by trade, from dependencies recorded at the grain where a redo happens","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","source":"@ajs, 2026-10-24, option (b) of reflow2:dec:idea-reflow2-becomes-the-web-of-rules-for-a-buildings-ifc-model; Seth's text message of 2026-10-23","statement":"A physical design (a building first) can record its parts at the grain where a redo happens, not every wall. For a building those are the units, the basement, the foundation, the structure, the excavation, egress, the MEP risers and each drawing sheet, joined by what depends on what, each dependency with its reason and source. A proposed change to one part (\"remove the basement storage and the two east units\") then returns what it reaches, grouped by trade (structural, geotechnical and excavation, architectural, MEP, code), with the calculations and sheets to redo, and says which dependencies were drawn by an agent and not yet checked by a person. The agent may draft the dependencies from the IFC model and the plan set; a person checks them. The redo list is only as right as the dependencies drawn, and it says so. Geometry stays in the model file (the 2026-10-13 dividing line); this holds consequences, not shapes. It is proven first on bhome or a copy. A real building's own dependencies (SeattleArch) are written only on its owner's word. The case this exists for is Seth's \"I'd redesign the building removing storage in basement and the two east units in the basement... It triggers a bunch of design 'redos'... engineering calcs, soil removal\".","status":"accepted"}
